newsitem.title: UK: Lord Gladwyn, British U.N. pioneer, dies at 96.
newsitem.headline: Lord Gladwyn, British U.N. pioneer, dies at 96.

text.p: Lord Gladwyn, who played a key role in drafting the United Nations Charter, died on Thursday, aged 96, British officials said on Friday.
He was acting secretary-general of the world body in 1946 until the appointment of the Norwegian Trygve Lie and served as permanent British representative.

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali paid tribute to him as "a man of great vision and commitment, who dedicated himself to promoting the United Nations ideals of peace and international understanding".
Born Hubert Miles Gladwyn Jebb, he went to the exclusive Eton boys school before obtaining an honours degree in history at Magdalen College, Oxford.
He entered the British diplomatic service in 1924 and towards the end of World War Two was in charge of a section of the Foreign Office known as the reconstruction department.

It was set up to work out Britain's foreign policies after the war and Gladwyn became engaged in drafting blueprints for the creation of the United Nations and other postwar international groups including the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
The first draft of the U.N. constitution was prepared under his direction. As acting secretary-general, he organised the first U.N. General Assembly meeting, which took place in London in 1946.
He served as ambassador to Paris from 1954 until his retirement in 1960, when was made a hereditary peer.
Boutros-Ghali said in a statement in New York that it was "particularly poignant that Lord Gladwyn should pass away on United Nations Day".

"As the first acting secretary-general of the United Nations and later as United Kingdom permanent representative to the United Nations from 1950-54, Lord Gladwyn made a crucial contribution to the work of the world organisation."
"At this time of great sorrow, I would like to express my profound regret at the passing of a great man, and my most sincere admiration for his extraordinary achievements."
Lord Gladwyn was survived by one son and two daughters. His wife Cynthia died in 1990.
